It has three branches:\n  - H6.1, averaging: a Lookahead sweep and a Fable-style EMA tail.\n  - H6.2, step count: batch 3072 with Lookahead cadence held fixed per example, to separate averaging from step size.\n  - H6.3, Muon constants: lr 0.20 with momentum 0.65, and Polar Express coefficients with update size matched. The second is pre-registered as a likely null.\n- **H2.5:** Newton-Schulz iteration cuts as a time lever.\n- **H1.2.7:** check the commits for the translate confound, then test block 3 at 576 vs 704 on the Muon tip with replication.\n- **H4.1.5:** translate 1 under Muon.\n- **H3.2.7:** tests whether E029's resize threshold comes from too little training at the 32 px test resolution, via a 32 px phase mid-run or a BN recalibration.\n- **H3.2.8:** a replicated head-to-head of resize vs epoch cuts.\n\n**Committee counterexamples**\n- **E013:** possibly the translate confound.\n- **E014:** within noise.\n- **E015:** per-step overhead.\n- **E016:** proxy launch overhead plus hard-example selection.\n- **E019:** block-1 time does not track its FLOPs.\n\nThe committee is wrong 60% of the time when it is unanimous, so its consensus shouldn't be trusted.\n\n**Top priority:** H1.1.3. Rerun E031 twice and E028 once, and pool them to measure the noise floor. E031's +0.21 pp margin triggered the loop's own rerun rule, which was skipped, and E032–E035 were judged against it."}

updates.statement: Sample efficiency dominates time-to-75%. An airbench-style whitened CNN (frozen patch-whitening, dirac init, BN, label smoothing 0.1, translate 2, alternating flip, Lookahead), with Muon on the block convs, 50% of steps at 24 px, block widths 128/256/704 and batch 2048, reaches 0.7551 in 8.75 epochs at 5.43 s (E031). That is far ahead of the best public CIFAR-100 result (8.11 s) and the organizers' ResNet9 (59 s). E031 is a single run with a +0.21 pp margin and has not been replicated. The SGD-era lever rates do not transfer to the Muon line (resize ~0.4 pp/s, epochs ~0.75 pp/s, block-3 width ~0.6 pp/s). Under Muon, cutting epochs costs ~0.56 pp per second saved (E031: 0.23 pp for 0.41 s). Resize near 50% has no usable measurement yet (E034: 0.75 +/- 1.2 pp/s). Resize at 75% costs ~1.8 pp/s (E029). Levers can only be ranked once the noise floor is measured.
updates.reason: The review flagged H1 as still written around the SGD-era E023 tip and its lever rates. Refreshed it to the Muon tip E031, fixed the unit error (0.31 is pp per epoch; the epoch-cut rate is 0.56 pp/s) and made the tip's lack of replication explicit.

updates.statement: The accuracy-vs-epochs slope is not a fixed property of the regime. It depends on the optimizer, architecture and recipe, and it flattens near the recipe's ceiling. Measured slopes: 0.87 pp/ep (E002, SGD, heavy regularization), 0.27-0.52 pp/ep (later SGD recipes), 0.29-0.31 pp/ep under Muon between 8.75 and 11 ep (E027, E031). The slope must be measured per recipe over spans of >= 2 epochs or with replicated endpoints. Interpolating it from another recipe is unreliable (E009, E034's misread rate).
updates.reason: E027 and E031 show Muon flattening the slope to ~0.3 pp/ep, which supports the claim that the slope depends on the recipe. Each of those slopes rests on single runs with ~0.3 pp difference noise, so the node stays open.

updates.statement: Noise floor on the Muon tip: rerunning E031 unchanged twice and E028 once, pooled with the originals, gives an sd of a 3-seed mean of about 0.15-0.25 pp and an sd of a run-to-run difference of about 0.25-0.35 pp, with same-seed nondeterminism dominating. If the pooled E031 mean falls below 0.7535, the tip reverts to E028 and E032-E035 are re-judged against the pooled baseline. From then on, any |delta| < 2 x sd(diff) is inconclusive.
updates.reason: The review notes that the H1.1.3 rerun rule fired on E031 (+0.21 pp margin) and was skipped, and that E032-E035 were stacked on it. Re-anchored the test to E031/E028. This is the top-priority experiment, because every verdict since E023 depends on it.

updates.statement: Accuracy per FLOP is block-specific. Block-2 width (the largest FLOP share, 16x16) is cheap to cut (E012: 384->256 cost ~0.2 pp with +1 ep). Block-1 width binds (E019: 128->96 lost 0.52 pp but saved only 0.74 s, so block-1 time is not proportional to its FLOPs, probably because it is bandwidth-bound at 32x32). The claim that block-3 width binds rests only on E021 (+0.33 pp for 576->704, about 1 sd of a difference). That result may also be confounded with translate 4->2: the descriptions disagree on E013's translate. All of this was measured under SGD, and none of it has been re-checked on the Muon tip.
updates.reason: Lowered confidence. The only block-3 evidence (E021) is within ~1 sd and possibly confounded with translate (review). E019, a committee counterexample, is explained here by block-1 cost not tracking FLOPs. All evidence is SGD-era.

updates.statement: On the Muon tip E031 (128/256/704), using 2 convs per block instead of 3 (all else fixed, epochs raised so that time matches E031 within 0.1 s) gives 3-seed accuracy at least equal to E031's within the measured noise floor. In other words, depth per block is a cheaper lever than epochs.
updates.reason: Re-anchored from the obsolete SGD tip E023 to the Muon tip, as the review asked.

updates.statement: Block-3 dose-response on the Muon tip E031: widening block 3 from 704 to 896 (head input matched, nothing else changed) raises 3-seed accuracy by >= 0.3 pp at <= +0.35 s. That is a rate >= 0.85 pp/s, which beats the ~0.56 pp/s cost of cutting epochs under Muon.
updates.reason: Re-anchored to E031 and benchmarked against the Muon epoch rate. Confidence lowered because the E021 evidence is weak and possibly confounded.

updates.statement: Cutting block 2 from 256 to 192 on the Muon tip E031 (128/192/704, nothing else changed) saves >= 0.3 s and loses <= 0.2 pp, i.e. <= 0.6 pp/s, about the epoch-cut rate under Muon.
updates.reason: Re-anchored to the Muon tip. Muon orthogonalizes the block-2 filters, so the cost of narrowing them may differ from the SGD-era measurement.

updates.statement: If the current net lacks the original airbench96 residual over the last two convs of each block (x = x + x0), adding it raises 3-seed accuracy on E031 by >= 0.3 pp at <= +2% time. Check the code first.
updates.reason: Re-anchored to the Muon tip. No new evidence.
No change. Already refuted, and its lineage is SGD-era.

updates.statement: Per-step work that does not scale with resolution is a growing share of time on the Muon tip. E031 averages ~25 ms per step over ~210 steps at batch 2048. Of that, ~1.66 ms is Muon (~0.95 ms Newton-Schulz bmm plus ~0.7 ms of small elementwise kernels, E026). Lookahead, BN and elementwise kernels, augmentation, interpolate and host gaps between graph replays add more. Removing this work (fewer or cheaper Newton-Schulz iterations, a whole-run graph) cuts time directly at equal math.
updates.reason: The step-time numbers were stale (9-14 ms SGD steps). Updated them to the Muon/bs2048 tip using E026's Muon cost breakdown, as the review asked.

updates.statement: A torch.profiler run of E031 (a few hundred steps at each of 24 and 32 px) shows >= 2.0 ms per step of time that does not scale with resolution: the Muon Newton-Schulz and elementwise kernels, the SGD+Lookahead foreach updates, augmentation, interpolate, index gathers and host gaps. That is >= 10% of a 24 px step. The profile also records the actual Newton-Schulz iteration count (3 or 5).
updates.reason: Re-anchored to the Muon tip. The review and D009 both put this profile first. It is a prerequisite for H2.5 and H2.4.4.

updates.statement: On E031, capturing the whole training run (or each resolution phase) as one CUDA graph cuts mean time by >= 4%, with |delta accuracy| within the noise floor, and lowers the 24 px / 32 px step-cost ratio to <= 0.62. In this design, augmented batches are staged into per-step buffers by batched kernels inside the timed train (precomputing outside the timed region is illegal), and the LR, Lookahead and Muon scalars come from a GPU table.
updates.reason: Re-anchored to the Muon tip. Fulcrum's measurement (0.575x with a whole-run graph vs ~0.65-0.82x with plain compile) remains the prior. Added the legality constraint flagged in the search audit.
No status change. E022 showed fused optimizer updates help (-2.3%). H2.4.3 and H2.4.4 are re-anchored to the Muon tip.

updates.statement: Low-resolution steps are cheaper but less useful, and their cost depends on the optimizer and is nonlinear in the low-res fraction. Under SGD, 33-50% at 24 px cost ~0.4 pp per second saved (E008, E013, E018). Under Muon, 75% at 24 px cost ~1.8 pp/s (E029), which points to a threshold once the 32 px phase gets short. Near 50% under Muon the cost is unmeasured within noise (E034). Data filtering is dead (E016).
updates.reason: E029 contradicts the linear ~0.4 pp/s claim. Rewrote H3 as optimizer-dependent and nonlinear, and lowered confidence.

updates.statement: Progressive resizing: a 24 px step costs ~0.68x a 32 px step under per-step graphs (E008). Under SGD, 33-50% schedules lost ~0.4 pp per second saved, independent of antialias (E008, E013, E018). The cost is nonlinear above ~50%: E029 (75% at 24 px under Muon) lost 1.36 pp, which suggests the run needs >= ~4-5 epochs at the 32 px test resolution, while LR is still meaningful, for features and BN statistics to adapt. Whether resize near 50% beats cutting epochs under Muon is unresolved (E034 +0.18 pp for +0.24 s is within noise).
updates.reason: E034 moved from + to ~: the review shows its rate (0.75 +/- 1.2 pp/s) was compared with a mis-unitized epoch rate. E029 added as evidence of a threshold. Confidence lowered from 0.65.
E029: 70-75% at 24 px lost 1.36 pp (0.7438), far off the ~0.4 pp/s line and infeasible. The statement predicted feasibility and a linear rate.

E018 was infeasible (0.7512) at 0.42 pp/s, the same rate as the 50% schedule, so neither part of the prediction held. The notebook verdict already said refuted; the tree still listed it as inconclusive.
This was an SGD-era E004-base test (E017 came within 0.09 pp, which is within noise). The SGD resize line is obsolete under Muon.

updates.statement: On the Muon tip E031 (50% at 24 px), scaling translate to ~1 px during the 24 px phase only (2 px at 32 px) recovers >= 0.3 pp at equal time. Literature: lowering regularization at low resolution recovers resize loss (C0087/C0089).
updates.reason: Re-anchored to the Muon tip. Under Muon, E030 shows augmentation strength matters more (translate 4 cost -0.62 pp), which makes this mechanism more plausible.

updates.statement: Conditional on H2.4.4 (whole-run graph, 24 px step <= 0.62x), a 24/28/32 curriculum by thirds on the Muon tip, with >= 40% of steps at 32 px, loses <= 0.4 pp per second saved, below the ~0.56 pp/s Muon epoch-cut rate.
updates.reason: Re-anchored to the Muon tip and compared against the corrected epoch rate. Lowered slightly because the E029 threshold applies.

updates.statement: The airbench constants were tuned for long CIFAR-10 runs and are mis-tuned for a ~9-epoch 100-class run. Weakening regularization raised accuracy at fixed epochs under SGD (E004 +1.26 pp, E011 +0.35 pp), and the same holds under Muon (E030: translate 4 cost -0.62 pp). Muon on the block convs is the largest single optimizer lever found (+0.78 pp, E025/E026). Under SGD at >= 210 steps the run was sample-limited, and batch was a pure throughput lever (E015, E024, E028). Under Muon, step count binds below ~200 steps (E032). Schedule constants (whiten_bias_epochs 3, warmup, LR floor, Lookahead cadence) remain untested at this budget.
updates.reason: Folded in E025-E035. Muon reversed the prior expectation, and the unconditional 'batch is a throughput lever' claim fails under Muon (E032).

updates.statement: The best regularization strength scales with the epoch budget, under both SGD and Muon. At ~9-11 epochs the net under-fits, so weaker augmentation helps: cutout off (E004), translate 2 beats 4 (E011 +0.35 under SGD, E030 +0.62 under Muon). Label smoothing near 0.1 looks near-optimal (E014: LS 0 gave -0.31 pp, within noise). Translate 1 or 0 under Muon is untested.
updates.reason: E030 replicates the translate-2-over-4 direction under Muon, with a larger effect. E014 (a committee counterexample) is a single difference within noise, so it is relabeled ~ rather than treated as a refutation.

E011 (+0.35 pp under SGD) meets the 0.3 pp threshold but is within noise on its own. E030 independently shows translate 4 costing 0.62 pp under Muon. Two independent results agree in direction, so the node is supported.
The LS axis looks near-optimal: E014 (LS 0) gave -0.31 pp, within noise but in the wrong direction for this hypothesis. It was posed on the stale E004 SGD base. Low value.
It was premised on runs of >= 12 epochs. The Muon line is moving to fewer epochs (8.75), so the premise no longer applies.

updates.statement: Muon (Newton-Schulz-orthogonalized momentum, lr 0.24, momentum 0.6) on the block conv filters beats tuned Nesterov SGD on this airbench-style net for CIFAR-100. At ~11 epochs it gives ~+0.8 pp at equal epochs (E025 +0.78, E026 +0.84), and spending that gain on epochs gave the fastest feasible runs (E027, E031). This contradicts the public CIFAR-100 report (futurebiohackers PR #3: 'Muon lost to SGD').
updates.reason: The tree contradicted the results. E025 and E026 independently show ~+0.8 pp, more than 2.5 sd of a difference. E030 (augmentation) and E033 (lr) do not test Muon against SGD, so they move to H4.1 and H6.3.
Predicted >= +0.3 pp; got +0.78 (E025), replicated by fused E026 (+0.84).

updates.statement: Under SGD with per-example LR held fixed and >= ~210 steps, the run is sample-limited, not step-limited: batch 768 to 2048 leaves accuracy within noise (E015, E024, E028) and larger batches buy throughput (-3.1%, -3.9%). This does not hold unconditionally under Muon. Batch 3072 (~140 steps) lost 1.04 pp (E032). That loss is confounded by the Lookahead sync count and warmup length (both tied to steps) and by ~1.7% of images dropped per epoch in the partial batch.
updates.reason: Restated as SGD-only, as the review suggested. E032 contradicts the unconditional form under Muon, and its mechanism is untested (E033 changed lr at batch 2048, not 3072).
Answered by E024 (batch 1536 on the E021/E023 lineage): -3.1% time with flat accuracy, just short of the >= 4% threshold. The batch axis now continues under H6.2.

updates.statement: airbench schedule constants tuned for 37 epochs (or CIFAR-10 at 8 epochs) are off-optimal at ~9 epochs on CIFAR-100: warmup, LR end value, whiten_bias_epochs 3, momentum 0.85 and bias_scaler. The actual LR end value is disputed. The E035 post-mortem says the schedule ends at ~7% of peak, while H4/H4.5.1 assume decay to 0. The LR table in the tip commit must be read before any schedule test. Later CIFAR-10 records (hiverge, Fable) train the whitening bias for only 0.2 epochs.
updates.reason: E035 (Lookahead removal) tests averaging, not schedule constants, so it moved to H6.1. Added the LR-floor discrepancy flagged by the review.

updates.statement: After reading the actual LR end value in the E031 commit, an LR floor sweep on E031 (end at 0 vs the current value vs 15% of peak, changing nothing else) shows a spread of >= 0.3 pp across the three settings. The best setting differs from the current one.
updates.reason: Rewritten against the actual schedule, since the original '5% instead of 0' premise may be wrong (review). Re-anchored to the Muon tip.

updates.statement: On E031, cutting whiten_bias_epochs from 3 to 0.2 (nothing else changed) raises 3-seed accuracy by >= 0.3 pp at equal time. Training the whitening bias for ~1/3 of an 8.75-epoch run is a 37-epoch leftover, and the hiverge and Fable CIFAR-10 records both use 0.2 epochs.
updates.reason: Re-anchored to the Muon tip. The search found two independent records using 0.2 epochs.

updates.statement: Time-to-75% is set by the recipe's accuracy-per-step-cost curve. Optimizer geometry, averaging, regularization, resolution schedule and capacity together set both the per-epoch slope and the ceiling. Capacity value is block-specific (H1.2), but the evidence that block 3 / head features bind is weak and possibly confounded (E021). The cheapest feasible point keeps binding capacity, cuts low-value FLOPs and matches regularization to the epoch count.
updates.reason: Lowered slightly. The capacity-specific parts rest on the weak E021 evidence, and H6 now carries the optimizer and averaging part.
No new evidence. Its only Lvl3 is stale on the SGD base.
Framed on the obsolete E004 SGD base at 8-12 epochs. The interactions change under Muon (E030, E032, E035), so the result would not transfer to the tip.
Its premise (E021's block-3 gain) is about 1 sd and possibly confounded with translate. Lowered; it needs H1.2.7 first.

updates.statement: On the Muon tip, keeping block 3 at 576 and adding one 1x1 conv (576->1024, BN, GELU) before the final pooling reaches 3-seed accuracy >= E031's within noise at a lower mean time than E031.
updates.reason: Re-anchored to E031. It is conditional on H1.2.7 showing that block 3 matters at all.

updates.statement: On E031, concatenating global max and average pooling (doubling the head input, no conv change) raises 3-seed accuracy by >= 0.3 pp at <= +1% time.
updates.reason: Re-anchored to the Muon tip. Fulcrum found global max pooling gave no low-res robustness, a weak negative signal.
E005 (-0.41 pp) is about 1.4 sd of a difference, so it cannot close the node. It stays open pending the noise floor.

new.statement: Update geometry plus iterate averaging set sample efficiency on the Muon line. Muon's fixed-norm orthogonalized steps do not shrink near convergence, so (a) the iterate stays noisy to the end, which makes weight averaging (Lookahead, EMA tail) first-order (E035: removing Lookahead cost 0.81 pp), and (b) total movement scales with step count, so the number of steps (~200+) is a resource and batch increases past ~2048 lose accuracy (E032). The cheapest remaining margin should come from tuning averaging and Muon's own constants at zero per-step cost, and that margin can then be spent on epochs.
new.source: review (Lvl1 coverage: optimizer geometry and averaging); results (E025, E032, E035); search: arxiv.org/abs/2411.18704; arxiv.org/html/2507.01598v4

new.statement: Iterate averaging acts as the annealing that the short, high-LR Muon schedule does not fully provide. Stronger or better-placed averaging (Lookahead cadence and alpha, or a Fable-style EMA tail at an LR floor) raises accuracy at near-zero step cost.
new.source: results (E035 post-mortem); search: fable champion recipe (EMA tail every 4 steps, decay 0.7, LR floor 0.05); arxiv.org/abs/2411.18704

new.statement: On E031, a two-point Lookahead sweep (sync every k/2 steps, and separately a final alpha closer to the slow weights; current values read from code) raises 3-seed accuracy by >= 0.3 pp for at least one setting at <= +1% time.

On E031, adding a Fable-style EMA tail on top of Lookahead raises 3-seed accuracy by >= 0.3 pp at <= +1% time. The tail averages every 4 steps with decay 0.7, starts 8 steps before the decay ends, uses the EMA weights for eval and resets the EMA state in prepare.

Under Muon, the step count binds below ~200 steps, because each step moves the filters by a fixed orthogonalized amount and Lookahead syncs are counted in steps. E032's -1.04 pp at batch 3072 is partly an averaging effect (fewer Lookahead syncs, shorter warmup), not only fewer Muon steps.
new.source: results (E032, E033); review (E032 confounds); search: arxiv.org/html/2507.01598v4 (Muon critical batch size)

new.statement: On E031 at batch 3072, holding the Lookahead cadence and warmup fixed in examples rather than steps (and not dropping the partial batch) recovers >= 0.5 pp of E032's 1.04 pp loss. If it recovers < 0.2 pp, the loss is from Muon step count, and batch stays at 2048.
new.source: review (separate averaging from step size in E032)

new.statement: Muon's own constants (lr 0.24, momentum 0.6, fixed quintic Newton-Schulz coefficients, no update-magnitude schedule) come from airbench94_muon on CIFAR-10 and are slightly off-optimal here. The lr optimum is at or below 0.24 (E033: 0.32 cost 0.33 pp, within noise). The hiverge record uses lr 0.205, momentum 0.655 and an update magnitude that shrinks from 0.50 to 0.08.
On E031, Muon lr 0.20 with momentum 0.65 (hiverge values, nothing else changed) raises 3-seed accuracy by >= 0.3 pp.
new.source: search: hiverge baseline (lr 0.205, momentum 0.655); Fable (0.2255); results (E033)

new.statement: On E031, Polar-Express per-iteration Newton-Schulz coefficients at the same iteration count, with the update RMS matched to the current quintic's, change 3-seed accuracy by < 0.3 pp (a pre-registered likely null). Without RMS matching, the coefficient change is confounded with a hidden Muon lr change (C0118).

Muon's per-step cost (~1.66 ms/step, ~0.35 s per run on E031) can be cut at equal accuracy. Small conv filters tolerate looser orthogonalization (C0097, C0104), so fewer Newton-Schulz iterations, a cheaper polynomial, or fused elementwise kernels save time without losing accuracy per step.
new.source: results (E026 Muon cost breakdown); search: lit D009/D010 (C0097, C0104, C0115, C0116); arxiv.org/html/2512.04632 (Turbo-Muon ~1%)

new.statement: On E031, cutting Newton-Schulz by one iteration (e.g. 3->2 with aggressive per-iteration coefficients, or 5->3 if the code runs 5) saves >= 0.08 s per run with |delta accuracy| within the noise floor.
new.source: search: lit D009 (C0104, C0105); review (cut NS iterations after profiling)

new.statement: Diffing commits b0eba3b, 6d40ead and 12fffd2 settles whether E013 and E021 differ in translate amplitude. Independently, on the Muon tip E031, block 3 at 704 beats block 3 at 576 (time-matched by epochs) by >= 0.3 pp, pooled over 2 runs per arm. If not, the claim that block 3 binds (H1.2, H5.2) is dropped and 576 becomes the cheaper tip.
On E031, reducing translate from 2 px to 1 px (both resolution phases, nothing else changed) raises 3-seed accuracy by >= 0.3 pp at equal time, extending the E030 trend under Muon.
new.source: results (E030: translate 4 vs 2 cost -0.62 pp under Muon); review (translate 1 under Muon)

new.statement: E029's threshold comes from test-resolution mismatch, not from FLOPs removed. At 75% of steps at 24 px on E031, either (a) moving 32 px steps out of the low-LR tail (32 px for steps 40-65%, 24 px elsewhere) or (b) adding a short forward-only 32 px BN-statistics recalibration on training batches at the end of the timed train recovers >= 0.6 pp of E029's 1.36 pp loss.
new.source: search: lit D008 (C0079 FixRes); review (E029 discriminating test); results (E029)

new.statement: A head-to-head on E031 with replicated endpoints (2 runs each) compares two cuts. One is 50% vs 30% of steps at 24 px. The other is 8.75 vs 7.75 epochs. They give rates with errors under +/-0.3 pp/s, and resize near 50% costs >= the epoch-cut rate (~0.56 pp/s), so less resize plus fewer epochs is the faster frontier under Muon.
new.source: review (E034 unit mix-up and noise); results (E031, E034)

structured_output.summary:
I revised the tree with the Muon-era results E025–E035 and the review's corrections.

**Status and wording fixes**
- **Muon:** H4.2 and H4.2.1 are now supported at 0.85. E025 and E026 independently show about +0.8 pp, and E030 and E033 moved to the hypotheses they actually test.
- **Batch size (H4.4):** restated as true under SGD only, since E032 contradicts it under Muon. H4.4.2 is closed because E024 already answered it (-3.1%, just short of its 4% threshold).
- **Resize (H3 / H3.2):** rewritten as nonlinear and dependent on the optimizer. H3.2.5 is refuted by E029 and H3.2.3 is refuted by E018. E034 is relabeled inconclusive because the I047 rationale behind its comparison mixed units: 0.31 is pp per epoch, and the real epoch-cut rate under Muon is about 0.56 pp/s.
- **Translate:** H4.1.3 is supported. E011 under SGD and E030 under Muon agree in direction.
- **Block widths:** confidence in H1.2 and H5.2 is lowered. The only evidence that block-3 width matters, E021, is within noise and may be confounded with a translate change.
- **LR schedule (H4.5 / H4.5.1):** rewritten to first read the actual LR end value. The E035 post-mortem says about 7% of peak, while the tree assumed 0.
- **Retired:** stale nodes built on the old SGD bases (H5.1.1, H4.1.2, H4.1.4, H3.2.2).
- **Re-anchored:** the remaining open Lvl3s now point at the Muon tip E031, and H2's step-time numbers are updated to about 25 ms per step, of which about 1.66 ms is Muon.

**New hypotheses**
- **New Lvl1 H6:** Muon's fixed-size steps make step count and weight averaging first-order. This accounts for the Muon gain (E025), the cost of removing Lookahead (E035) and the batch-3072 loss (E032). It has three branches:
  - H6.1, averaging: a Lookahead sweep and a Fable-style EMA tail.
  - H6.2, step count: batch 3072 with Lookahead cadence held fixed per example, to separate averaging from step size.
  - H6.3, Muon constants: lr 0.20 with momentum 0.65, and Polar Express coefficients with update size matched. The second is pre-registered as a likely null.
- **H2.5:** Newton-Schulz iteration cuts as a time lever.
- **H1.2.7:** check the commits for the translate confound, then test block 3 at 576 vs 704 on the Muon tip with replication.
- **H4.1.5:** translate 1 under Muon.
- **H3.2.7:** tests whether E029's resize threshold comes from too little training at the 32 px test resolution, via a 32 px phase mid-run or a BN recalibration.
- **H3.2.8:** a replicated head-to-head of resize vs epoch cuts.

**Committee counterexamples**
- **E013:** possibly the translate confound.
- **E014:** within noise.
- **E015:** per-step overhead.
- **E016:** proxy launch overhead plus hard-example selection.
- **E019:** block-1 time does not track its FLOPs.

The committee is wrong 60% of the time when it is unanimous, so its consensus shouldn't be trusted.

**Top priority:** H1.1.3. Rerun E031 twice and E028 once, and pool them to measure the noise floor. E031's +0.21 pp margin triggered the loop's own rerun rule, which was skipped, and E032–E035 were judged against it.
